newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's PHIBOR rates mostly steady, one-week up.
newsitem.headline: Manila's PHIBOR rates mostly steady, one-week up.

text.p: Philippine interbank offered rates (PHIBOR) were mostly steady on Thursday, with only the one-week and two-month rates higher and the one year lower, traders said.
Dealers said the increase in the one-week rates were in line with the trend in the overnight money market.
Some banks had been temporarily covering their peso positions but most expected interest rates to soften in the long term due to the the cut in reserve requirements, a trader said.
The one percentage-point slash in reserve requirements will take effect on Friday, January 3 and another one percentage-cut will be implemented on July 4.
The rise in the two-month rates could just be a mere re-alignment, a trader said.
PHIBOR represents rates at which banks are willing to swap their pesos for dollars.
